page: Amazon Web Services x8i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Managed under the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading active at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8, alongside cryptographic accelerators like VAES and SHA-NI.

System memory capacity is 512.0 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5, yielding an allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle any local storage or hardware GPUs. Network throughput is backed by a 15 Gbps baseline connection. For storage persistence, external network-attached volumes are necessary due to the lack of onboard NVMe drives.

Benchmark outcomes show high single-core and multi-core capabilities, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 2,177.0 and a multi-core score of 17,920.0, both placing in the top quartile. Text processing performance reaches the top decile with a score of 2,903.0. Compression and decompression tests, such as single-threaded gzip (34.34 GB/sec) and multi-threaded bzip3 (225.97 GB/sec), perform strongly. CPU inference on smaller language models is efficient, reaching 374.11 tokens/sec text generation on 135M parameters, though generation speeds scale down significantly on large 70B parameter models (2.61 tokens/sec).

Given its high RAM-to-vCPU ratio and top-tier CPU-driven text processing, the x8i.8xlarge offers solid qualitative resource efficiency for memory-bound systems that do not require onboard high-speed local scratch disks. The server is well positioned for enterprise in-memory caches, large-footprint relational or transactional databases, real-time analytics, and high-throughput compression tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services x8i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with the x86_64 architecture, it contains a 480 MB L3 cache and supports AMX and AVX-512 instructions. The instance provides 512.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, equaling 16.0 GB per vCPU. It features no local storage or GPUs, relying on a 15 Gbps baseline network connection for persistence and communication. Benchmarks demonstrate strong performance in single-core and multi-core workloads, text processing, and data compression, as well as high static web throughput. Due to its dense RAM footprint and strong CPU capabilities, the instance fits in-memory databases, large cache layers, data processing, and enterprise memory-intensive applications.
